BUY_PREMIUM.label: Buy premium
BUY_PREMIUM.blurb: Options are cheap relative to how much this name actually moves. You want to be long optionality — pay a defined premium and let the move come to you.

SELL_PREMIUM.label: Sell premium
SELL_PREMIUM.blurb: Options are rich relative to realized movement. You want to be the seller — collect the premium and let time decay work, with the risk defined by long wings.

NEUTRAL_INCOME.label: Collect decay
NEUTRAL_INCOME.blurb: No cheap-or-rich edge outright, but the shape of the volatility curve pays you to own time in one expiry and sell it in another.

STAND_ASIDE.label: Stand aside
STAND_ASIDE.blurb: Nothing here is mispriced enough to pay for the risk. No trade is a position.

NO_DATA.label: Not priced
NO_DATA.blurb: No option chain was read for this ticker in this run, so no premium call can be made.

cheap.label: Cheap
cheap.detail: Implied volatility sits at the low end of this name's own range and near or below what it actually realizes. Long premium: straddles, strangles, debit spreads.

fair.label: Fair
fair.detail: Options are priced about right. Any trade here has to come from the chart or the term structure, not from the level of volatility.

rich.label: Rich
rich.detail: Implied volatility is high in its own range and well above realized. Short premium: credit spreads and iron condors, with defined risk.

unknown.label: Unknown
unknown.detail: The option chain wasn't priced for this name this run.

glossary.score: Setup Score, 0–100: how coiled the chart is right now — compressed Bollinger bandwidth, low realized-vol percentile, and an active TTM squeeze. It says a move is loading. It says nothing about direction.
glossary.iv_rank: IV Rank, 0–100: where today's implied volatility sits between the low and the high of the trailing year. Under ~25 is cheap, over ~65 is rich. Free data has no implied-vol history, so this is ranked against the name's own realized-volatility range — a proxy that reads a little high, because implied vol carries a persistent premium over realized.
glossary.iv_percentile: The share of the trailing year's volatility readings that sit below today's implied volatility. Same proxy caveat as IV Rank.
glossary.premium_score: 0–100 blend of IV rank (45%), the IV/HV risk premium (40%) and the term structure (15%). This is the number the buy-or-sell call is actually made on.
glossary.iv_hv_ratio: Implied volatility divided by realized. Around 1.1–1.2× is the normal risk premium; well above that is the market paying you to sell, well below it is a discount to buy.
glossary.vrp: Volatility risk premium: implied minus realized, in volatility points.
glossary.implied_move_pct: How far the option market is pricing this name to travel over the horizon, as a percentage of spot.
glossary.hist_move_pct: The same move estimated from realized volatility instead. The gap between the two is the edge.
glossary.term_structure: Front-expiry IV against a later one. Contango (later is pricier) is normal. Backwardation means the market expects something soon — it favours selling the front month or running a calendar.
glossary.skew: Out-of-the-money put IV minus call IV, in vol points. Fat put skew means the put side pays more to sell than the call side.
glossary.liquidity: How tradable the chain is, from the at-the-money bid/ask spread and open interest. Wide markets quietly cost more than the edge is worth, so thin names get simpler structures or none at all.
glossary.pop: Model probability of finishing in the profit zone, from a zero-drift lognormal at the chain's own implied volatility. An estimate, not a guarantee — and a high probability of a small win is not the same as a good trade.
glossary.credit_to_width: Credit collected divided by the width of the spread. Under ~20% you are being paid too little for the risk.
glossary.em_pct: One-sigma expected move over the horizon from realized volatility. Roughly 68% of outcomes land inside ±1σ, 95% inside ±2σ.
glossary.squeeze: The TTM squeeze: Bollinger Bands sitting inside the Keltner Channels. On means energy is building; fired means it just released, which is the actual entry trigger.
glossary.lean: A faint directional hint from squeeze momentum. A tiebreaker between two structures, never a reason to take a position.
glossary.earnings: Calendar days to the next report. Inside the expiry, IV is elevated for a reason and collapses the morning after — that cuts both ways depending on which side you're on.
glossary.debt_cash_ratio: The Shariah financial screen: interest-bearing debt and cash as a share of market cap, both required under ~33%.

playbook.long_straddle: Buy the at-the-money call *and* put. You win if the move is big enough, either way; you lose if it sits still. The trade for cheap options in front of a coiled chart.
playbook.long_strangle: Buy an out-of-the-money call *and* put. Cheaper than a straddle and needs a bigger move to pay — the budget version of the same both-ways bet.
playbook.bull_call_spread: Buy a call, sell a higher one. A capped, cheaper bullish bet — the short leg pays for part of the long one.
playbook.bear_put_spread: Buy a put, sell a lower one. A capped, cheaper bearish bet.
playbook.iron_condor: Sell an out-of-the-money call spread *and* put spread. You collect premium and keep it if price stays between them. Defined risk on both sides.
playbook.short_strangle: Sell an out-of-the-money call and put with no wings. Collects more than a condor, but the loss is open-ended — margin-heavy, experts only.
playbook.bull_put_spread: Sell a put, buy a lower one. You collect credit and win if the stock stays above the short put — a bullish way to be short rich premium.
playbook.bear_call_spread: Sell a call, buy a higher one. You collect credit and win if the stock stays below the short call.
playbook.calendar_spread: Sell the near expiry, buy the same strike further out. Profits when the front decays faster than the back — the trade for an inverted term structure.
playbook.covered_call: Against shares you already own, sell a call above the price. Turns rich premium into income and caps your upside at the strike.
playbook.stand_aside: No edge worth paying for. The best trade is often none.
playbook.shares_only: Trade the underlying instead of options.
playbook.no_data: No usable option chain this run — nothing to price.

disclaimer.general: Educational tool, not financial advice. Expected-move bands and probabilities are statistical estimates from past and implied volatility — not predictions. Option prices are last-known mids and will have moved; price every trade in your broker before placing it.
disclaimer.compliance: Not a fatwa. The halal screen covers the underlying company (industry plus debt and cash ratios, AAOIFI / S&P Islamic style), not the instrument. Conventional options are themselves contested in Islamic finance — selling them, trading on margin and short selling draw the most objection. Seek your own ruling, and re-verify each name with a dedicated screener (Zoya, Musaffa).
disclaimer.method: Indicators are computed without look-ahead: every value uses only data up to and including its own bar. IV rank and percentile are proxies ranked against realized-volatility history, because free data sources do not publish implied-volatility history.
